subject: Latency & compliance tradeoffs — EU/APAC hosting options
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@euhealth.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today’s call

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of constraints you shared:
- EU-only patient data storage for PII and model inputs (primary legal requirement)
- Significant APAC user base (Singapore & Sydney) with latency sensitivity for interactive features (~ < 300ms target)
- Procurement needs SOC2 + network diagram and a draft MSA redline window of ~3 weeks

What we recommend (qualification + tradeoffs):
1) Hosted (Redwood API) — EU region: fastest time-to-value and minimal ops. Meets EU residency if traffic and storage are pinned to EU region, but note: cross-region caching or backups to non-EU regions would need to be disabled. Latency to APAC users will be higher than local hosting — recommend edge routing + regional fallbacks.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool in EU) — good middle ground: predictable throughput and data isolation within EU. Lower latency vs multi-tenant hosted (for sustained workloads) and supports VPC peering for tighter network control.
3) Private (VPC or on-prem) — required if legal/regulator insists on customer-controlled network and on-prem data egress restrictions. Best for strict residency but adds ops and longer lead time (2–6+ weeks depending on customer's infra).

Proposed next steps: 
- I’ll attach a short comparison matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and a draft mutual action plan. (See attachments.)
- Can you confirm whether encryption keys must be customer-managed (KMS/HSM) or Redwood KMS is acceptable for the initial pilot?
- If procurement wants SOC 2 evidence, Rafael will share our SOC 2 report and network diagram; can procurement@euhealth.ai receive that doc?
- If you’re open, schedule a brief network/infra call with your cloud/networking lead next week to validate VPC peering options and latency targets.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the KMS answer and preferred time for the infra call and then loop in Rafael for the SOC 2 pack.

Best,
Markus
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

Attachments: redwood-hosting-comparison-20270507.pdf (summary), proposed-map-routing.png (latency map), EUH-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft MAP)

From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@euhealth.ai>

Cc: procurement@euhealth.ai
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 14:33:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today’s call

Thanks Markus — helpful summary. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: Regulator requires that all patient-level inputs and derived embeddings be stored and retained only within the EU. Backups may be allowed in another EU country but not outside the EU.
- KMS: For Phase 1 pilot, external KMS is preferred (customer-managed keys). We will confirm if HSM is required for Phase 2.
- Latency: For our clinicians in APAC, interactive latency > 400ms becomes noticeable. If Hosted EU results in median 600–800ms, that will negatively impact adoption.

Procurement asked if you can provide:
1) SOC 2 report and network diagram (send to procurement@euhealth.ai)
2) A short note on whether Dedicated in EU would allow customer-managed KMS and VPC peering (yes/no + any constraints)

We’d like to run a short pilot for a single clinical workflow (approx 30k tokens/day). Can you include an estimate of expected token cost delta between Hosted EU and Dedicated (monthly)?

I can join a network call next Tue 11–12 CET. Please confirm.

— Sophie
Head of Product, EU Health AI

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today’s call

Hi Sophie — looping in a couple clarifications on Dedicated vs Private from an ops/security perspective (short bullets):

- Dedicated (EU region):
  • Supports customer-managed KMS via BYOK integration with most major cloud KMS providers — we can document the exact flow for your security team.
  • VPC peering available for Dedicated capacity in most EU regions; egress still flows through controlled routes but data residency (at-rest) remains in the EU pool.
  • Latency: For sustained workloads, Dedicated can reduce median tail latency vs multi-tenant Hosted due to reserved GPU pools and colocated placement; however, it won’t be as low as an APAC-local deployment. Expect ~20–40% lower token latency versus Hosted EU for steady traffic patterns.

- Private (VPC/on-prem):
  • Provides full network isolation and can be configured to prevent any cross-border backups or egress.
  • Lead time is longer (depends on customer infra readiness). We offer an on-prem appliance and a VPC-hosted private control plane option.
  • Ops overhead: customer is responsible for some infra patching/maintenance in certain private deployments.

Preliminary cost note (very rough, ballpark for pilot):
- Hosted EU: baseline (low ops) — estimated ~$1.2k/month for the pilot workload (30k tokens/day)
- Dedicated EU: higher fixed commitment but lower per-token at scale — estimated $2.5k–3.0k/month (includes reserved capacity premium)
- Private: setup costs add to monthly; initial setup could be $8k–15k + monthly infra costs depending on topology

We’ll prepare a one-page cost/latency comparison and attach it to the MAP. Rafael — I’ll need the SOC 2 pack and network diagram to share with Sophie/procurement.

Thanks,
Laura
VP, Product Ops — Redwood Inference
